chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā عليه السلام, he said:

I asked him about a man who performs the obligatory prayer in which the recitation is done aloud: is it required of him not to recite aloud? He said: If he wishes, he may recite aloud, and if he wishes, he may refrain from doing so.
So this report is in agreement with the generality, and we do not act upon it; rather, practice is based on the first report.

key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: the generality, i.e. the non-Shi'i majority
key_terms.الْعَمَلُ: the adopted practice or legal application

ai.seo_question: Is reciting aloud in the obligatory prayers of audible recitation optional or obligatory?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of reciting aloud in obligatory prayers where audible recitation is prescribed. Although the report appears to allow a choice, the compiler states that it conforms to the view of the generality and is not acted upon, with practice instead based on the first report affirming the obligation of jahr.
